core_obligations: Identify the target as the formal spectrum of a complete weakly admissible ring (proof lines 6543-6545).
Use that the closed immersion is representable and affine to conclude that the source is affine and countably indexed (proof lines 6545-6549).
Write the source as a formal spectrum of a ring of the same kind, and apply the McQuillan case to see that the immersion corresponds to a taut map with dense image (proof lines 6549-6554).
Conclude from the dense image criterion that the map is surjective, so that the source is a quotient by a closed ideal (proof lines 6554-6557).

difficulty_reason: For a closed immersion of formal algebraic spaces into a countably indexed affine formal algebraic space, the lemma asserts that the source is again a countably indexed affine formal algebraic space and that the immersion corresponds to the quotient of the ring by a closed ideal (statement lines 6533-6541). The proof identifies the target with the formal spectrum of a complete weakly admissible ring using the description of countably indexed spaces, then uses that a closed immersion is representable and affine to conclude from the statement on affine morphisms that the source is affine and countably indexed (proof lines 6543-6549). Writing the source as a formal spectrum of a ring of the same kind, it applies the corresponding result for closed immersions into a McQuillan space to see that the immersion is given by a taut ring map with dense image (proof lines 6549-6554), and then concludes from the criterion that a continuous taut map with dense image between these rings is surjective, so that the source is a quotient by the kernel, which is closed (proof lines 6554-6557). The claim is H2: the argument chains three named results but each link is a stated consequence with its reason -- the type of the source from affineness of the immersion, the shape of the ring map from the McQuillan case, and surjectivity from the dense image criterion -- and the closedness of the kernel is read off from the conclusion.
